A queued rate that never decays across many restarts means division is not making progress and the corpus is not shrinking - correlate with the leaf byte-overflow and snapshot-capture panels, not with container memory headroom. outcome=immediate alone, with queued and sole_occupancy flat at zero, is the healthy steady state: the budget is never contended and the gate is invisible. outcome=sole_occupancy is a DIFFERENT PREDICATE from queued and is read differently (issue #2844): the hydration was serialised because its largest CONTIGUOUS allocation was too large to attempt alongside anything else, which does not improve with a bigger memory grant - every byte-denominated bound here is derived from that grant and admits more concurrent work as it rises. Read a sustained sole_occupancy rate as a signal to divide leaves or lower MaxLeafBytes, and specifically NOT to provision more memory. ABSENT IS NOT ZERO. These targets omit the or vector(0) fallback, because a literal zero would draw a healthy estate identically to a build that does not carry the gate at all, and those call for opposite responses. All three arms are instead PRE-MINTED at zero the first time a tree is seen in the process, carrying the exact tag set a later admission carries, so a flat zero line is a MEASURED zero and a missing line means the build did not land. The budget is derived from the heap hard limit and is deliberately NOT configurable: a bound an operator has to set cannot rescue a process that is already restart-looping.

panels.title: Resident leaf working-set sheds (rate) by class - issue #2767 (absent = build did not land)
panels.description: Leaf activations deactivated by the per-silo RESIDENT leaf working set so the hydrated population stays under its derived byte budget (orleans.lattice.leaf.residency.sheds), split by whether the shed leaf was snapshot-banked or unbanked. READ THIS PANEL DIRECTLY ABOVE THE HYDRATION ADMISSIONS PANEL, BECAUSE THE TWO BOUND DIFFERENT QUANTITIES AND NEITHER SUBSTITUTES FOR THE OTHER. The admission gate (issue #2765) bounds how many hydrations run CONCURRENTLY, which caps the PEAK cost of each one. It says nothing about what survives them. LeafSnapshotHydrationSource retains the whole encoded snapshot frame for the lifetime of the activation, so a completed hydration leaves roughly one frame resident and a forced blocking compacting gen2 collection reclaims NONE of it while the activation lives. The steady state therefore grows with the number of LIVE ACTIVATIONS, not with concurrency, and was entirely unbounded - which is why the heap hard limit was still reached with the admission gate provably binding (queued 238 against 9 immediate). kind=banked is the bound working at its cheap end: the shed leaf had a snapshot, so it reloads cheaply when next touched. kind=unbanked IS THE ARM TO ACT ON. It means the working set has run out of snapshot-backed candidates and is buying headroom by evicting leaves that must pay a whole-window WAL replay to come back, so a sustained rate points at SNAPSHOT COVERAGE and not at this bound - raising the budget would not help and lowering it would make it worse. Shedding is a GRACEFUL deactivation, so a shed leaf captures a snapshot on the way out and an unbanked shed converts itself into a banked candidate for next time; that is what makes the banked-first preference drain rather than recirculate, and it is why a healthy estate trends towards banked. ABSENT IS NOT ZERO. These targets omit the or vector(0) fallback, because a literal zero would draw an estate that never needed to shed identically to a build that does not carry the bound at all. Both arms are instead PRE-MINTED at zero when a tree first registers, carrying the exact tag set a later shed carries, so a flat zero line is a MEASURED zero and a missing line means the build did not land. The budget is derived at runtime from the heap hard limit and is deliberately NOT configurable, for the same reason the admission budget is not.

panels.title: Resident leaf working-set budget (bytes) - issue #2788 (absent = build did not land)
panels.description: The byte budget the per-silo resident leaf working set is actually enforcing (orleans.lattice.leaf.residency.budget_bytes). THIS PANEL EXISTS TO MAKE A ZERO SHED COUNT READABLE. The shed counter directly below reads zero both when the bound is correctly quiescent and when it cannot engage at all, and those have opposite remedies. READ THIS AGAINST THE CONTAINER MEMORY GRANT. A budget of the same order as the whole grant means the process dies before the threshold can ever be reached, so the bound is present, plausible-looking and doing nothing - which is exactly what issue #2788 fixes. Originally the budget was derived from GCMemoryInfo.TotalAvailableMemoryBytes alone, on the assumption that it reports zero when no heap hard limit is configured. It does not: it reports HOST PHYSICAL MEMORY, so on a large host running a small container the derivation produced a budget larger than the grant. The budget is now the smaller of the heap hard limit and the cgroup memory limit, divided by four, floored at 64 MiB, and falls back to 1 GiB only when NEITHER ceiling can be observed. A flat line at exactly 1073741824 therefore means both detections failed and should be investigated as a detection defect, not read as a tuned value. This is a GAUGE and not a counter on purpose: a counter observes an action and could only ever report that a shed happened, while the question an operator has here is about STATE - what bound is in force - which a counter structurally cannot answer at any level of priming.

panels.title: Resident leaf working-set resident bytes - issue #2788 (absent = build did not land)
panels.description: Bytes currently accounted to live, un-shed leaf registrations in the per-silo resident leaf working set (orleans.lattice.leaf.residency.resident_bytes). STACK THIS AGAINST THE BUDGET PANEL ABOVE: the ratio between the two is the headroom, and it is the only reading that distinguishes an estate comfortably under bound from one about to start shedding. A resident figure pinned near the budget with a steady shed rate below is the bound working. A resident figure that stays a small fraction of the budget while the process is dying of memory exhaustion means the budget is too large to be a bound at all - compare the budget line against the container grant rather than concluding that leaf residency is not the cost. A resident figure that is FLAT AT ZERO while leaves are demonstrably activating means registration is not happening, which is a wiring defect and not quiescence; the registrations panel below separates those two.

panels.title: Resident leaf working-set registrations - issue #2788 (absent = build did not land)
panels.description: Leaf registrations currently held by the per-silo resident leaf working set (orleans.lattice.leaf.residency.registrations). THIS IS THE PANEL THAT SETTLES WHETHER A ZERO SHED COUNT IS QUIESCENCE OR A DEAD LEDGER. An empty ledger and a populated ledger that is correctly under budget are indistinguishable on the shed counter, because a counter reports events and both of these are the absence of an event. A non-zero registration count with zero sheds is the bound populated and under budget, which is healthy. A registration count that is FLAT AT ZERO while the silo is activating leaves means the registration path is not running at all and the bound is inert, which is a defect. Priming the shed counter at zero per tree fixed present-and-zero versus absent and could not fix this, because the instrument observes the action while the question is about the state.

panels.title: Leaf snapshot capture concurrency peak (silo high-water) - issue #2696 (absent = build did not land)
panels.description: Greatest number of leaf-snapshot captures observed running CONCURRENTLY on one silo since process start (orleans.lattice.leaf.snapshot.capture.concurrency_peak) - issue #2696. THIS IS THE ONE CAPTURE QUANTITY NO OTHER PANEL ON THIS DASHBOARD CAN SHOW. Every other capture series is written around the per-leaf single-flight guard, which is an instance field on ONE activation: it stops a leaf capturing twice at once and is blind by construction to how many DIFFERENT leaves are capturing against the one shared snapshot storage provider. A thousand leaves each passing their own guard is exactly the fan-out issue #2696 describes and it registers nowhere else. READ IT AS A LEVEL, NOT A RATE, AND DO NOT EXPECT IT TO FALL. The series is monotone non-decreasing by design, so a spike is reported by the scrape that observes it AND by every scrape afterwards; that is what makes it immune to scrape timing rather than merely unlikely to be missed by it. PR #2723 deferred this metric because an INSTANTANEOUS gauge of the current depth is sampled only when the endpoint is scraped, so the transient spike that makes the reading worth having is precisely what falls between two scrapes - that objection was correct and is why this is a high-water mark. A histogram was equally unavailable: this container renders every histogram as _sum and _count with no buckets and no quantiles, so only the mean survives, and a mean dilutes a spike to nothing - one capture at depth 64 among ten thousand at depth 0 reads as 0.0064. A restart is what clears the peak. THE TARGET DELIBERATELY OMITS or vector(0). The gauge is registered at host build from AddLattice rather than on first capture, so a silo that has never captured still publishes the series: a flat zero line is a MEASURED zero and a MISSING line means the build did not land. Substituting a literal zero would draw those two identically. There is no tree tag and that is deliberate - the maximum spans every leaf on the silo and the contended provider is itself silo-wide, so a per-tree split would report several smaller numbers, none of which is the depth the provider actually saw. Read it beside the concurrent-entries panel below: this one says how deep it got, that one says how often it happens, and a peak alone cannot separate a single transient spike during startup from sustained contention.

panels.title: Leaf snapshot captures admitted under contention (rate) by tree - issue #2696
panels.description: Leaf-snapshot captures admitted across the attempt boundary while at least one OTHER capture was already in flight on the same silo (orleans.lattice.leaf.snapshot.capture.concurrent_entries) - issue #2696. It is the FREQUENCY half of the cross-leaf concurrency reading whose magnitude half is the peak gauge above, and the pairing is load-bearing rather than decorative: a high-water mark alone cannot distinguish one transient depth of 3 during startup from a silo sitting 3 deep continuously for an hour, and those are opposite operational states that call for opposite responses. DO NOT READ THE already_in_flight DECLINE REASON AS A PROXY FOR THIS SERIES. That reason counts a capture the per-leaf guard TURNED AWAY because the same leaf was already capturing; this counts a capture that was ADMITTED while a DIFFERENT leaf was capturing. The two populations are disjoint - one never reaches the attempt boundary and the other is past it - and only this one describes real concurrent load on the shared provider. A deployment can show a high decline rate with zero entries here (one hot leaf, no cross-leaf contention) or the reverse (wide fan-out, every leaf capturing once), and the two demand different fixes. Zero-primed per tree: the instrument adds 0 on an uncontended attempt, so a flat zero is measured absence of contention rather than a tree whose captures never ran.

panels.title: Leaf snapshot segment reads (rate) by tree/outcome - issue #2914
panels.description: Individual leaf-snapshot SEGMENT frames read during a segmented hydration, split by outcome (orleans.lattice.leaf.snapshot.segment_reads) - issue #2914. A snapshot whose encoded frame exceeds LeafSnapshotSegmentBytes is no longer stored in one BLOB column: the payload is split into row-aligned segments, each a standalone frame in its own grain-state row, and hydration folds them one at a time. That split is the whole bound. The contiguous allocation that failed in issue #2844 is materialised by the storage provider COLUMN READ, before any lattice code runs and before deserialization, so bounding it requires bounding the column, and the only way to bound a column is to stop putting the whole payload in one. CHART missing AND failed SEPARATELY AND ALERT ON EITHER, because they are different questions with different answers: missing means the manifest references a segment that is not there, which is a DURABILITY signal, while failed means the read threw, which is an I/O signal. Both fail the hydration CLOSED - the cache is emptied and the rehydrate declines, so the leaf replays its whole readable WAL rather than activating with a snapshot silently holding fewer rows than its coverage claims, which is the one shape that would let coverage-gated WAL GC trim the last durable copy of a prefix. THE TARGET DELIBERATELY OMITS or vector(0). All three arms are pre-minted at zero, but priming runs INSIDE the segmented fold, so the series exists only once a segmented hydration has actually run on this silo. That makes presence itself the signal, and substituting a literal zero would draw the segmentation-has-never-run-here case and the segmentation-ran-and-read-nothing case identically. Read an ABSENT series as either the build not landing or no snapshot yet exceeding the window; read a FLAT ZERO as the fold having been entered for that tree.

panels.title: Leaf snapshot segmented hydrations completed (rate) by tree - issue #2914
panels.description: Activation-time leaf-snapshot hydrations that folded a SEGMENTED snapshot to completion (orleans.lattice.leaf.snapshot.segmented_hydrations) - issue #2914. This is the population for which the contiguity bound was actually exercised: an ordinary leaf whose snapshot fits inside LeafSnapshotSegmentBytes is stored and hydrated inline and is never counted here, so this series names exactly the leaves that would previously have demanded a single contiguous array of the whole payload. READ IT AGAINST THE sole_occupancy ARM OF orleans_lattice_leaf_snapshot_hydration_admissions, WHICH SHOULD FALL AS THIS RISES: the admission gate added for issue #2844 refuses an oversized contiguous claim, and this change stops the claim being oversized in the first place, so the two are complementary rather than redundant and the gate is deliberately retained. It is counted only on a COMPLETE fold, so it is NOT an attempt count and must not be read as one: a hydration that declined partway appears on the missing or failed arms of orleans_lattice_leaf_snapshot_segment_reads and never here, which keeps the how-many-segmented-snapshots-hydrated-successfully question and the how-many-segment-reads-went-wrong question from sharing a population they do not share. THE TARGET DELIBERATELY OMITS or vector(0), for the reason given on the segment-reads panel above: priming runs inside the fold, so an absent series and a measured zero are different readings and a literal zero would draw them the same.

panels.title: Leaf snapshot segment peak bytes (high-water) by tree - issue #2914
panels.description: HIGH-WATER mark of the largest single contiguous segment frame this process has materialised while hydrating a segmented snapshot, per tree (orleans.lattice.leaf.snapshot.segment_peak_bytes) - issue #2914. THIS IS THE PANEL THAT ANSWERS WHETHER THE BOUND HELD. It must stay at or below the configured LeafSnapshotSegmentBytes window however large the underlying snapshot grows, so a value above that window is the direct signal that segmentation is not bounding what it claims to bound, and is the correct thing to alert on. READ IT AS A LEVEL, NOT A RATE, AND DO NOT EXPECT IT TO FALL: the series is monotone non-decreasing within a process lifetime, which is what makes it immune to scrape timing rather than merely unlikely to be missed by it, and a restart is what clears it. It is a high-water gauge and DELIBERATELY NOT A HISTOGRAM: this container renders every histogram as _sum and _count with no buckets and no quantiles, so the only reading available would be a mean, and a mean dilutes the single large allocation the instrument exists to catch into an average of many small ones. THE TARGET DELIBERATELY OMITS or vector(0). Unlike the silo-wide capture-concurrency peak, this gauge is NOT registered at host build - it is keyed by tree and primed on the first segmented hydration for that tree, so an ABSENT series means either the build did not land OR no snapshot has yet exceeded the segment window on this silo. Those two are not distinguished here, and substituting a literal zero would additionally collapse them into the measured-zero case.

panels.title: WAL replay gate occupancy: ceiling, available, queued - issue #3047
panels.description: Occupancy of the per-silo WAL replay concurrency gate, as three series that are only interpretable together. CEILING is the denominator the permit family previously lacked: a SemaphoreSlim does not expose its own maximum and the gate is sized once and never re-created or topped up, so one permit withheld from sixteen (noise) and one withheld from two (half this silo's replay throughput) were indistinguishable on a scrape. A ceiling of 0 is an unambiguous not-yet-sized sentinel, never a sized gate, because the sizing resolver returns the configured value when positive and the derived default otherwise and both are at least 1. AVAILABLE is the headroom a new activation would find; a zero is ambiguous between an unsized gate and a saturated one and is resolved only against the ceiling, which is why the two are charted together. QUEUED is the un-terminated set, and it is the only series here that can show a gate admitting nothing: every other permit instrument records at a terminal outcome downstream of the wait - the queue-wait histogram on acquisition or cancellation, the replay counters once a permit is held - so an activation that never acquires and is never cancelled records nothing anywhere, and a permanently saturated gate renders byte-identically to a tree that never activated a leaf. Available cannot substitute for it: that count saturates at zero and reports the same figure for one waiter and for a thousand. Read the panel as the width of the door, whether it is open, and the queue outside it. An absent series means the build does not carry the instruments; a queued series pinned above zero while available sits at zero is a saturated gate with a standing backlog, and on an otherwise idle gate it is the signature of a leaked decrement rather than of real demand (issue #3047).

panels.title: Leaf snapshot capture-DRIVER declines (rate) by reason - issue #3185 (minting rate of frozen floor holders)
panels.description: Capture DRIVERS that declined to drive a leaf-snapshot capture at all (orleans.lattice.leaf.snapshot.driver.declines), split by reason - issue #3185. THIS IS NOT THE CAPTURE-DECLINES PANEL ABOVE AND THE TWO MUST NEVER BE SUMMED. orleans.lattice.leaf.snapshot.capture.declines counts declines raised INSIDE CaptureSnapshotCoreAsync, so its declines and the attempt counter partition that method's invocations exactly; these are raised in a CALLER THAT NEVER REACHED IT, so folding them together counts a strict superset and corrupts the decline-versus-attempt ratio that counter exists to report. THE TARGETS ARE ORDERED DELIBERATELY AND THE PANEL IS NOT A SIX-ARM BREAKDOWN. Target A isolates reason=deactivate_unproven_coverage_stale, which is the MINTING RATE of the frozen floor-holder population that blocks WAL reclamation estate-wide; the remaining arms are collapsed into target B behind a reason!= matcher so that deactivate_unproven_coverage_current - which dominates on a healthy estate, because it is the harmless decline through the same gate by the same predicate - cannot bury the one arm that carries signal. That burial is the exact failure the arms were split to prevent, and a panel plotting all six together would reintroduce it at the presentation layer. A leaf deactivating on the stale arm carries a projection checkpoint above its durable snapshot coverage and neither advanced a checkpoint over cache-resident applies nor cold-rebuilt its cache from the WAL start, so it cannot honestly stamp coverage: THE DECLINE IS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR AND NOT A FAULT, and what is charted is a rate rather than an error. Target C overlays the WAL GC drive's completion rate on the same axis so the crossing is visible without arithmetic; the ratio panel below states the same comparison as a single number. reason=deactivate_unproven_unclassified means the classifier itself threw and should be zero outside a test harness - it is a sink kept separate so neither informative arm can silently absorb an unknown. The three benign recheck_* arms are periodic-recheck gates that were previously silent and are charted for completeness, not as a health signal. THE FOURTH, reason=recheck_no_durable_checkpoint, IS THE OPPOSITE AND IS DRAWN ON ITS OWN TARGET D FOR THE SAME REASON TARGET A IS SPLIT OUT - issue #3300. It means the leaf holds rows and NO partition has ever reached a durable checkpoint, so every capture driver is simultaneously unsatisfiable and the tree is making nothing durable at all. Before it existed that state was counted as recheck_coverage_current, the arm whose meaning is 'every partition's coverage already matches its checkpoint' - vacuously true at -1 == -1, and materially the worst state available, which is how a tree that had never made anything durable came to be indistinguishable in every counter from one that had made everything durable. IT MUST NOT BE LEGENDED BENIGN AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED BACK INTO TARGET B: doing so reinstates exactly that burial at the presentation layer, which is the failure this panel's target split already exists to prevent. A non-zero value on target D is a DATA-LOSS-RISK signal, not a rate to tune - the leaf's rows are readable only while the process lives. Expect it to fall to zero once the starvation drive it triggers supplies the missing checkpoint; a value that persists across many scrapes means the drive is running and not advancing, which is a different defect and points at the WAL read path rather than at this gate. FALSIFIABLE CONSEQUENCE, worth checking before acting on this series: the frozen population is believed to consist of leaves that died WITHOUT running their deactivate hook, because the stale shape is by construction unreachable from inside the activation that observes it - every internal route that advances a checkpoint also latches the no-loss signal that OPENS this gate and heals the leaf. If the stale arm instead tracks ordinary deactivation volume, that model is wrong and the remedy moves to the activation path. ABSENT IS NOT A MEASURED ZERO HERE, WHICH IS AN EXCEPTION TO MOST PANELS ON THIS DASHBOARD: this instrument is NOT zero-primed, matching its capture.declines sibling, so a series appears only on the first decline and a missing line is consistent BOTH with a build that lacks the instrument AND with one that carries it and has declined nothing. Confirm deployment from the image digest, never from the presence of this series. TARGET E, reason=recheck_checkpoint_stalled, IS THE SECOND DATA-LOSS-RISK ARM AND IS SPLIT OUT FOR EXACTLY THE SAME REASON AS TARGET D - issue #3389. It is the COMPLEMENT of target D, not a duplicate of it: D is a leaf that has NEVER reached a durable checkpoint, whereas E is a leaf that reached one and then STOPPED ADVANCING. The frozen leaf is the more dangerous of the two and the harder to see, because it hydrates cleanly on restart and satisfies every eligibility gate, so before this arm existed it reported recheck_coverage_current forever: coverage and checkpoint are frozen EQUAL, which makes checkpoint > covered false for the same vacuous reason -1 > -1 is false. Writes accepted after the freeze are acknowledged, served correctly from the live activation, and LOST ON THE NEXT RESTART. IT MUST NOT BE LEGENDED BENIGN AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED BACK INTO TARGET B. Expect it to fall to zero once the starvation drive it triggers advances the checkpoint; a value that persists across many scrapes means the drive is running and not advancing, which points at the WAL read path rather than at this gate. Note that a frozen leaf can drive retained WAL to ZERO rather than growing it, because compaction keeps reclaiming entries the checkpoint never banks, so an empty WAL is NOT evidence of health on a tree showing this arm.

panels.title: Frozen floor-holder minting vs WAL GC drive completion (ratio; ABOVE 1 = divergent) - issue #3185
panels.description: The single number that decides whether WAL reclamation converges: rate(orleans.lattice.leaf.snapshot.driver.declines{reason=deactivate_unproven_coverage_stale}) divided by rate(orleans.lattice.wal.gc.blocked_leaf_reactivations) - issue #3185. THE THRESHOLD IS 1 AND IT IS NOT A TUNING KNOB. Above 1 the frozen floor-holder population is minted faster than the WAL GC reactivation drive discharges it, so the population grows without bound and NO drive-side tuning converges - the mismatch is asymptotic rather than a matter of constants, because the drive is bounded per sweep behind a per-consumer cooldown while minting is bounded only by collection rate. Raising a per-sweep cap multiplies a bounded term and leaves an unbounded one unbounded; it buys a slower divergence, which is worse than no change because a halved growth rate reads as progress. Below 1 the drive is merely slow and tuning genuinely applies. THIS PANEL EXISTS BECAUSE THE COMPARISON WAS PREVIOUSLY DONE BY HAND, and a quotient computed by eye from two rate panels is exactly the reading that goes wrong: both terms are rates over a window, so eyeballing two lines on different scales silently substitutes a visual impression of slope for a division. READ IT AS A LEVEL AND NOT AS A TREND - it is already a ratio of two rates, so a second differentiation is meaningless. The denominator is clamped so a drive that has completed nothing in the window cannot produce a division by zero; a numerator above zero against a clamped denominator therefore renders as a large finite value rather than as a gap, which is the correct reading - minting with no discharge at all is the most divergent state available, not an absent one. THAT READING HOLDS ONLY WHERE THE NUMERATOR IS NON-ZERO, AND THE QUIET-TREE CASE IS THE OPPOSITE OF IT. On a low-traffic tree both rates fall to zero for long stretches, because the drive is reactivation-driven and a tree with no traffic generates no reactivations to discharge anything; the quotient then renders as 0 and draws as perfect health on a tree that may be permanently stranded. A near-zero value on a quiet tree therefore means NO DRIVE ACTIVITY, NOT CONVERGENCE. This panel cannot see strandedness on such a tree at all, and no per-tree ratio can, because strandedness there is a statement about passes that reclaimed nothing rather than about a rate: read orleans.lattice.wal.gc.passes{outcome="stranded"}, which advances with zero reclaim independently of tree size - a 1 MB tree is as stranded as a 922 MB one, so a small volume is not evidence of a small problem. DO NOT QUOTE THIS PANEL AS EVIDENCE OF HEALTH FOR ANY TREE WHOSE NUMERATOR IS FLAT AT ZERO; on that population it is silent rather than reassuring, and the two render identically. NEITHER SERIES IS ZERO-PRIMED on the numerator side, so an absent line here does NOT establish that the build lacks the instruments; confirm deployment from the image digest. Do not compare this ratio against WAL BYTE totals to corroborate it: compaction reclaims DEAD bytes on a sawtooth whose envelope can fall while this ratio sits above 1, because the floor stall holds RETAINED bytes, which no compaction arm may discard. The two quantities move independently and a falling WAL is not evidence that this ratio is healthy.

panels.title: Leaf deactivation BARRIER failures by barrier - issue #3366 (a teardown step threw and was contained)
panels.description: Deactivation barriers that threw during OnDeactivateAsync (orleans.lattice.leaf.deactivation.barrier.failures), split by which barrier faulted - issue #3366. WHAT THIS MEASURES IS A CONTAINMENT EVENT, NOT A CRASH. A leaf teardown runs four ordered barriers - digest_publish, checkpoint_flush, snapshot_capture, frontier_pin - and before this instrument existed they shared one try/catch, so the FIRST barrier to throw cancelled every barrier after it and the whole teardown reported nothing at all. A faulting checkpoint flush therefore silently suppressed the snapshot capture that would have preserved the leaf's rows, which is the mechanism by which a GRACEFUL restart destroyed recently-written durable entries. Each barrier now fails independently and is counted here, so a fault is both survivable and attributable. READ THE reason TAG AS THE REMEDY SELECTOR, because the four are not interchangeable. checkpoint_flush is the expected arm and the one implicated in #3366: it means the projection checkpoint could not be persisted at teardown, so the leaf's durable coverage is behind its in-memory state and the rows written since the last checkpoint survive only if the snapshot barrier below it succeeded. snapshot_capture is strictly worse - the flush may have succeeded but the blob that would have carried the uncheckpointed tail was not written, so those rows are unrecoverable after the process exits. digest_publish and frontier_pin are internally best-effort and realistically cannot throw; a non-zero value on either means an invariant inside those paths is violated and is a defect report, not a rate to tune. DO NOT READ A NON-ZERO VALUE HERE AS THE CAUSE OF A DATA LOSS ON ITS OWN. It establishes that a barrier faulted and that the barriers after it still ran, which is precisely the distinction that was unavailable before: an absent snapshot can now be attributed to a declining capture (orleans.lattice.leaf.snapshot.capture.declines), to a barrier that threw (this instrument), or to the hook never running at all (no series on either), and those three have materially different remedies. Pair it with orleans.lattice.leaf.snapshot.capture.declines{reason="no_tree_id"} on the same window: the two together partition the silent-teardown population that #3366 was opened against. ABSENT IS NOT A MEASURED ZERO. This instrument is NOT zero-primed, matching its capture.declines and driver.declines siblings on this dashboard, so a series appears only on the first fault and a missing line is consistent BOTH with a build that lacks the instrument AND with one that carries it and has torn down cleanly every time. Confirm deployment from the image digest, never from the presence of this series. A HEALTHY ESTATE IS FLAT AT ABSENT, so any line at all here is worth reading.

panels.title: WAL GC blocked-consumer population (uncapped)
panels.description: Latest distinct durable consumers blocking the cursor floor, per tree and silo. Denominator for orleans.lattice.wal.gc.blocked_leaf_reactivations: read the population trend beside heal/drive outcomes to distinguish backlog drain from arrivals outpacing drain; neither signal alone establishes convergence. Partition pins are distinct consumers, not distinct leaves. The scan continues past the eight-id report cap even when every partition is blocked; this changes diagnostics only, never trim entitlement. Registry-present pins, offset-covered zero pins and proven-empty abstained partitions are excluded. Offset-plane population gaps are included once. Zero is primed on the first pass; -1 means the census could not be established, not an empty population. No cross-silo sum: multiple silos may observe the same durable pins. Values remain at the latest census until the next pass; use the scheduler phase-age panel to detect stalled collection.

panels.title: Leaf checkpoint-flush TAIL failures by step - issue #3393 (a post-flush notification threw and was contained)
panels.description: Notification steps that threw AFTER the checkpoint flush itself succeeded (orleans.lattice.leaf.checkpoint.flush.tail.failures), split by which step faulted - issue #3393. READ THIS PANEL BESIDE PANEL 163, NOT INSTEAD OF IT, because the two measure different halves of one named thing. The checkpoint_flush barrier on 163 covers the BODY - the durable write - and stands down once that write lands. The tail runs three notifications after it (cursor_report, inline_digest_publish, snapshot_recheck), each contained separately and deliberately so, because under issue #2220 a failed notification tearing down the activation produced a replay loop. That containment is correct and this instrument does not change it; what it changes is that the fault is now countable. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR READING 163 IS THE WHOLE POINT: a checkpoint_flush count of ZERO on 163 does NOT establish that the checkpoint path is healthy. On the drain captured under #3393 the barrier counter read zero for checkpoint_flush while 1,699 dirty digests died inside this tail, so the barrier counts are a FLOOR on the damage, not a total. inline_digest_publish is the arm that fired in production and means a leaf's parent was never told its digest changed, so the tree's upward digest chain is stale until the next mutation re-drives it - which on a quiescing tree may be never. snapshot_recheck means the post-flush re-evaluation of snapshot need did not run, so a block pin can retain the tree's shared WAL and is a candidate contributor to unbounded WAL growth (issue #3094). cursor_report DESERVES A SPECIFIC WARNING: the reporter call is ALSO wrapped in its own per-partition try/catch inside ReportCursorIfActiveAsync, so only the option lookup and consumer-id construction around it can reach this counter. A ZERO ON cursor_report IS THEREFORE NOT EVIDENCE THAT CURSOR REPORTING IS HEALTHY; it is double-contained and its ordinary failures are invisible here by construction. ABSENT IS NOT A MEASURED ZERO. This instrument is not zero-primed, matching its barrier sibling on 163, so a series appears only on the first fault and a missing line is consistent BOTH with a build that lacks the instrument AND with a build that carries it and has drained cleanly. Confirm deployment from the image digest, never from the presence of this series. A HEALTHY ESTATE IS FLAT AT ABSENT, so any line at all here is worth reading.

panels.title: Leaf span FAIL-OPEN commits by reason/origin - issue #2125 (out-of-span key kept locally; absent = healthy or build did not land)
panels.description: Keys a leaf committed LOCALLY although its declared [low, high) span excludes them, because declared-span admission found no neighbouring leaf to forward them to (orleans.lattice.leaf.span_fail_open_commits) - issue #2125. Split by reason (no_sibling: the chain pointer on the key's side is null; self_reference: it names the leaf itself) and origin (client_write, merge, cross_shard_migration). WHY IT MATTERS: WAL replay admits by declared span, so a row committed outside its leaf's span is one that leaf will not reinstate on its own rebuild; whether it survives a cold restart depends on the checkpoint position of the leaf that does declare it. A fail-open is the shape that precedes a silent loss. READ THE ORIGIN TAG FIRST: cross_shard_migration is the deliberate graft shape and can be expected during a reshard; client_write or merge is an accidental fall-back and is worth investigating on its own. A leaf that declares no span at all (a single-leaf tree or a bulk-loaded leaf) owns every key and never advances this counter, so a bulk-loaded tree reading absent is not evidence its chain is healthy. ABSENT IS NOT A MEASURED ZERO. This counter is not zero-primed, so a series appears only on the first fail-open and a missing line is consistent BOTH with a build that lacks the instrument AND with a build that carries it and has never fallen open. Confirm deployment from the image digest, never from the presence of this series. A HEALTHY ESTATE IS FLAT AT ABSENT, so any line at all here is worth reading. The companion warning log (rate-limited to one line per silo every 10 seconds) names the leaf and tree.
